sentence: This project uses fluorescence microscopy to see molecular targets inside live cells and tissues at the nanoscale.
This project compares breast cancer screening results from 3D mammogram reading with and without an AI tool in a randomized clinical trial.
This project uses clinical and molecular data to study how aortic stenosis with and without atherosclerosis differs in its biology and risk.
This project studies what helps sedentary Pacific Islander adults start and keep up physical activity, looking at neighborhood and social environments.
This project designs, builds and tests a trans-nasal system for transesophageal echocardiography that requires no anesthesia.
This project uses neuroimaging and machine learning to sort tinnitus into subtypes based on dynamic functional connectivity of brain networks.
This project studies which modifiable risk factors drive clonal expansion and malignant transformation to hematologic malignancy in a community of older adults.
This project checks whether blood-based proteomic assays can accurately detect pancreatic cancer.
This project uses imaging mass cytometry and machine learning on patient tongue biopsies to find immune features that predict malignant transformation in oral dysplasia.
This project builds a knowledge graph from clinical data, imaging data and literature to find factors that increase or lower dementia risk.
This project builds a point-of-care instrument that quickly checks whether bone marrow aspirate samples are adequate without destroying them.
This project tests how single amino acid changes in proteins alter the function of stem cell derived cardiac muscle cells.
This project studies how nicotine and HIV lead to breakdown of the blood-brain barrier, neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in the brain.
This project studies how coagulation factor XII is recruited and activated at the platelet surface.
This project develops a wearable sensor and an AI system that alerts patients and physicians to dangerous changes in breathing and the environment.
This project tests whether N-glycan analysis of urine can track progression to lupus nephritis and how patients respond to treatment.
This project builds a data analysis center that uses proteogenomic data to better understand cancer biology and improve cancer treatment.
This project studies whether losing a mitochondrial kinase blocks mitochondrial transport into dendrites of cultured mouse and human neurons.
This project uses protein-based nanopore technology to build a portable system that measures two tuberculosis biomarkers for diagnosis and treatment monitoring.
This project studies transcriptional alterations in post-mortem brain samples to learn the role of the ubiquitin pathway in a late-onset neurodegenerative disorder.
